title: Living and dead faith are one species; charity adds only external relative perfection
source_text: XII. Quodcunque vero discrimen constituant Scholae Romanae Theologi inter fidem vivam & mortuam, formatam & informem, nolunt tamen illas esse diversas fidei species, sed accidentali tantum perfectione inter se differre, & utramque esse unam & eandem specie fidem. Nempe fidei accidit, ut modo charitati conjuncta reperiatur, quandoque ab ea separatim existat, quod fidei est essentiale in utroque statu retinens, & a charitate quum adest accipiens perfectionem solum externam atque respectivam.
pass_a_gloss: But whatever discrimination the Theologians of the Roman School constitute between living and dead faith, formed and unformed, they nevertheless do not will those to be diverse species of faith, but to differ among themselves only by accidental perfection, and both to be one and the same faith in species. Namely it happens to faith that it is sometimes found joined to charity, sometimes exists separately from it, retaining what is essential to faith in either state, and receiving from charity when present only an external and relative perfection.
pass_b_english: Rome refuses to make living and dead faith different species: they differ only by accidental perfection and remain one faith in species.
Faith may be found with or without charity while keeping its essence; charity when present adds only an external, relative perfection.

lemmas.gloss: only an external and relative perfection

choices.why: Roman unity of faith across states.
